extracted.intended_audience: CGPDTM (Indian Patent Office) officials, patent attorneys/agents, and other Indian IP stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Practical comments and suggested wording for amendments to the Manual of Patent Office Practice and Procedure (India), addressing AI inventorship, accessibility, examination/hearing practice, and opposition procedure. Intended to guide drafting of procedural and substantive guidance in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on AI inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual should provide clarity on whether AI can qualify as an inventor under the Patents Act, 1970, considering statute, procedure, court judgments, and legislative history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BananaIP's conclusions to be reflected in the Manual: (a) the objective of the patent system is to incentivize human ingenuity and creativity; (b) Sections 6 and 7 require an applicant to be a true and first inventor who can voluntarily transfer rights, has a limited life period that ends when she/he is deceased, and can affix signatures on relevant forms — all possible only if the inventor is a human being; (c) tests for patentability include persons with ordinary skill and human intervention benchmarks; (d) courts have held the objective of patent law in India is to encourage inventive activity and ingenuity of human beings. Suggestion: The Manual should clearly state that only human beings qualify as true and first inventors under Section 6 of the Patents Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of IP Office systems and processes to persons with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a dedicated section in the Manual recognizing need to facilitate accessibility of website, processes, and systems to persons with disabilities and to provide reasonable accommodations, in line with the Guidelines for Accessibility and Reasonable Accommodations (4 March 2022) and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested paragraph and specific operational obligations for controllers, examiners, and officers: (i) provide accessibility measures and reasonable accommodations as per the guidelines and statute; (ii) provide accommodations recommended by the designated nodal officer; (iii) acknowledge accessibility-related communications within 24 hours and confirm whether requested measures/accommodations will be provided; (iv) give written reasons if a requested accommodation cannot be provided without undue delay, considering statutory timelines; (v) not require payment of a fee for processing accessibility requests or for providing reasonable accommodations such as adjournment or time extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination reports: clarity, analysis, and limits on new objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should give clear, reasoned analysis when raising objections based on statutory provisions and/or prior art, and the Manual should set rules on when new objections may be raised during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify two recurring problems: (a) lack of analysis when raising statutory/prior-art objections that leaves applicants guessing what the examiner meant; (b) raising new objections after the first statement of objections without issuing a subsequent examination report. Suggested guidance: include specific guidelines on approach, format, and analysis of statutory provisions and prior art in examination reports; establish a mechanism for raising new objections that reinitiates examination while affording applicants opportunities to respond; provide for a bar on new objections at stages after the first examination report (e.g., at hearing) unless a subsequent examination report is issued, to ensure fairness and natural justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit citing new prior art or new objections at hearing stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing notices and conduct should not introduce new objections or previously un-cited prior art at the hearing stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested Manual language: clearly state that it is not permitted to cite new prior arts or new objections at the hearing stage. Rationale: this enables compliance with statutory and natural justice requirements and brings predictability and certainty to the hearing process. Tie this prohibition to corresponding rules on when new objections may be raised (see Examination reports criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and post-hearing orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual should set clear timelines for issuance of orders following hearings and for completion of other adjudicatory steps to improve predictability and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify current lack of timelines for issuance of orders after hearings as an issue. Suggested inclusion: specific timelines for issuance of orders following hearings; timelines within which Controllers are required to complete opposition proceedings (see Opposition Process). Timelines should be stated to improve transparency, efficiency, and legal compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjournment protocols and handling missed hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify procedures and timelines for filing and deciding adjournment requests, and protocols for hearings missed by hearing officers or attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested guidance to be included in the Manual: clear protocols for adjournment requests and related decisions (how to apply, grounds accepted/rejected, timelines for decision), and processes to be followed when hearing officers or attorneys fail to attend scheduled hearings (e.g., rescheduling rules, recording of non-attendance, remedies for affected parties). This addresses concerns about process clarity and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and selection of opposition board members; publication of constituting orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase transparency in opposition proceedings by publishing the order constituting the opposition board and by providing guidance on selection of board members (competence in applicable patent provisions and relevant technology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current problems noted: (a) order constituting the opposition board is not published so parties do not know board composition until report is given; (b) no guidance on how board members are picked or on expected expertise; (c) opposition proceedings are not time-driven. Suggested Manual changes: require that the order constituting the opposition board be made available to the parties and published online as part of prosecution history; include criteria and a selection process for board members (expectation of legal and technical competence appropriate to the technology at issue); and set timelines within which Controllers must complete opposition proceedings to ensure transparency, quality, and predictability.
